name: Plesetsk Cosmodrome
tagline: Russia's northern military cosmodrome — more launches than any other site
description: Plesetsk Cosmodrome lies in Russia's far north, at about 62.9°N. It was founded in 1957 as an R-7 intercontinental-missile base and became a space launch site on 17 March 1966, when a Vostok-2 rocket put Kosmos 112 into orbit from Site 41/1. Run by the Russian Ministry of Defence, it launched most Soviet military satellites — reconnaissance, navigation, early-warning and Molniya communications — and by 1997 had made more than 1,500 launches, more than any other site in the world. R-7 family rockets flew from Sites 41/1, 16/2 and 43; Kosmos-3M and Rokot from Sites 132 and 133; Tsyklon-3 from Site 32; and, since 2014, Angara from Site 35. Site 43 has its own entry.
best_known_for: Russia's northern military cosmodrome — over 1,500 launches by 1997, more than any other site
